title: DTOs Mimicking Domain Models in the Application Layer
pattern: Application services acting as a "bargain-basement Bounded Context" by assembling and performing business rules directly on combinations of raw boundary DTOs.
why_bad: It leads to domain model anemia and leaks context definitions. It turns the application layer into a procedural transaction script, locking rules away from the core model.
detection: Application layer classes managing business logic by combining and evaluating fields from multiple distinct DTO payloads.
counterexample: Thin orchestrators whose single role is combining already-computed values for view builders.
fix: Map DTOs to their respective domain types first, coordinate them within the domain model, and return a clean domain-grounded view.
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 14, p. 532).
